items.q: 4-2-1 rule for severe nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy means what?
o: Severe haemorrhages in 4 quadrants, venous beading in 2, IRMA in 1
items.exp: High risk characteristics predict imminent proliferation; closer review with panretinal laser threshold follows while macular oedema treats in parallel.

items.q: New vessels on the disc in diabetic eye need which definitive retinal therapy?
items.exp: Scatter laser sacrifices peripheral retina to save disc and macula from bleeding and traction; anti VEGF adjuncts clear blood for laser completion.
items.kp: New disc vessels: burn periphery to save centre.

items.q: Hard exudate plaque threatening fovea with OCT thickening in diabetic is what and treated how?
o: Diabetic macular oedema; anti VEGF with focal or grid laser
items.exp: Leaking microaneurysms and diffuse breakdown swell macula silently; intravitreal therapy with laser dries while glycaemic and pressure control sustain.
r: Correct. Macular oedema, inject and laser.
items.kp: Fat fovea in diabetic: inject and spot laser.

items.q: Grade IV hypertensive retinopathy is defined by which added feature?
o: Disc swelling atop haemorrhages, cotton wool and exudates
items.exp: Malignant hypertension oedemas the disc with systemic emergency (renal, cardiac, neuro); urgent pressure lowering with cause hunt follows. Lower grades observe with control.
items.kp: Swollen disc plus high pressure: malignant hypertensive eye.

items.q: Florid retinal haemorrhages with poor vision and afferent pupil defect after CRVO indicates which type and risk?
o: Ischaemic with rubeosis and 100 day glaucoma risk needing scatter and iris watch
items.exp: Extensive nonperfusion predicts anterior segment new vessels; prophylactic laser with monthly iris checks and anti VEGF bridges prevent painful blindness.
items.kp: Blind pupil plus bloody retina: ischaemic, iris will sprout.

items.q: Pale retina with cherry red spot and boxcarring after sudden painless blindness is what?
o: Central retinal artery occlusion needing minutes scale pressure lowering
items.exp: Inner retinal infarction spares choroidal foveal blush; massage, paracentesis and acetazolamide bridge while arteritis and carotid hunts run. Ninety minute window decides fate.
items.kp: Pale with cherry centre: artery shut, minutes count.

items.q: Giant cell arteritis must be excluded in CRAO by which tests and action?
o: ESR with CRP and urgent steroids when suspected
items.exp: Arteritic occlusion blinds the fellow eye within days; steroids start on suspicion before biopsy while embolic workup continues. Jaw claudication and scalp tenderness warn.
items.kp: Blocked artery in elderly with scalp pain: steroids first.

items.q: Midperipheral dot haemorrhages with dilated veins, low pressure and rubeosis in carotid stenosis is what?
o: Ocular ischaemic syndrome needing carotid revascularisation
items.exp: Chronic hypoperfusion mimics diabetic changes with hypotony and anterior segment ischaemia; Doppler with endarterectomy or stenting restores flow while PRP tames new vessels.
items.kp: Starved eye with low pressure: open the carotid.

items.q: Smokestack leak on angiography with neurosensory detachment in stressed young man on steroids is what?
o: Central serous chorioretinopathy settling mostly with steroid stop
items.exp: Choroidal hyperpermeability lifts macula blurring centre; stopping steroids with observation cures most while chronic cases get photodynamic or mineralocorticoid therapy.
items.kp: Stressed steroids plus blurred spot: serous leak.

items.q: Copper versus silver wiring of retinal arterioles signifies what?
items.exp: Thickened walls reflux copper then silver as sclerosis advances; AV nicking companions confirm chronicity while acute florid changes mark malignant phases.
items.kp: Metallic wires in retina: years of pressure.
